title: MailPlus Setup Assistant: run Synology MailPlus Server without a fixed IP using Cloudflare
body:
Self-hosting email on a home Synology NAS used to mean paying your ISP for a static IP, fighting residential IP blocklists, requesting PTR reverse DNS, and hoping TCP port 25 wasn't blocked. **[MailPlus Setup Assistant](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoMailPlusSetupAssistant/)** lets you run your own **Synology MailPlus Server** with Cloudflare handling the internet-facing mail leg — **no fixed IP, no IP reputation headaches, free inbound receiving, and low-cost outbound sending on Cloudflare's Workers Paid plan** — while you keep using the exact same MailPlus web, mobile, and IMAP/SMTP experience you already know. --- ## How It Works Under the Hood Before installing anything, here is the exact architecture MailPlus Setup Assistant sets up when you choose the Cloudflare route. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Internet Sender[Remote Mail Server] Recipient[Recipient Mail Server] end subgraph Cloudflare["Cloudflare Edge (Your Cloudflare Account)"] ER["Email Routing
(MX on your domain)"] Worker["Inbound Email Worker
(auto-created by Assistant, no spool)"] VPC["Workers VPC Service
(auto-created by Assistant, TCP 25)"] ES["Email Sending
(smtp.mx.cloudflare.net:465)"] end subgraph NAS["Your Synology NAS (Behind Home Router / No Open Ports)"] Tunnel["Cloudflare Tunnel
(reused from Syno Connect Center)"] MP["Synology MailPlus Server
(SMTP 25 on LAN IP)"] Relay["Local Mail Relay
(127.0.0.1:2525, STARTTLS)"] UI["MailPlus Web / Mobile / Clients"] end Sender -->|"Inbound SMTP"| ER ER --> Worker Worker --> VPC VPC -->|"Encrypted Tunnel"| Tunnel Tunnel -->|"LAN IP :25"| MP UI <--> MP MP -->|"STARTTLS + Local Auth
127.0.0.1:2525"| Relay Relay -->|"Implicit TLS :465
AUTH PLAIN (api_token)"| ES ES -->|"DKIM / SPF / DMARC signed"| Recipient ``` You can also inspect this exact inbound/outbound pipeline interactively inside MailPlus Setup Assistant by expanding **How Cloudflare mail works** on the Overview page: ![Interactive How Cloudflare mail works diagram in Receive mode showing Internet, Email Routing, Email Worker, VPC Service, Tunnel, and MailPlus Server](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f37883b8-d4cb-4ca8-bfc0-7690aec21cfa) ### Who manages what? - **Created and managed automatically by MailPlus Setup Assistant:** The **Inbound Email Worker**, the **Workers VPC Service**, the Email Routing rules, the Email Sending onboarding, and the required DNS records are all created automatically inside your Cloudflare account during setup — you do **not** have to write, deploy, or maintain them yourself. When you click **Remove…**, the Assistant deletes only what it created. - **Reused from Syno Connect Center:** The **Cloudflare Tunnel** is **not** created by MailPlus Setup Assistant. For **receiving mail**, the Assistant discovers and reuses the healthy Cloudflare Tunnel in your Cloudflare account set up by **[Syno Connect Center](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoPkgConnect/)** (connected to your own domain — not a temporary quick tunnel), without modifying or deleting your Tunnel configuration. - **Sending mail does not need a Tunnel:** Outbound mail goes directly from MailPlus through the local relay to Cloudflare's SMTP endpoint over TLS port 465. ### 1. Receiving mail (Inbound: Internet → Cloudflare → MailPlus) 1. **Cloudflare Email Routing** publishes Cloudflare's MX, SPF, and DKIM records on your Cloudflare-hosted domain so incoming mail from the internet arrives at Cloudflare first. 2. **An Inbound Email Worker** (automatically deployed to your Cloudflare account by MailPlus Setup Assistant) receives each incoming message. You choose one of two modes during setup: - **Whole domain automatically (recommended):** Uses a catch-all rule pointing to the Worker. MailPlus Server itself decides whether each mailbox exists, so adding or removing MailPlus users later requires no extra steps. - **Chosen mailboxes:** Creates exact routing rules for your MailPlus users. Whenever you add or remove MailPlus users, press **Sync mailboxes** on the Overview page to update the rules. 3. **Workers VPC Service + Syno Connect Tunnel:** MailPlus Setup Assistant discovers the healthy Cloudflare Tunnel in your account from Syno Connect Center (read-only; it never changes or deletes your tunnel) and automatically registers a **Workers VPC Service** targeting MailPlus Server's TCP port 25 on your NAS's private LAN IPv4 address (never `127.0.0.1`, so MailPlus's Postfix loopback trust cannot be abused as an open relay). 4. **Direct streaming with zero intermediate storage:** The Worker streams each email byte-for-byte over the VPC Service directly into MailPlus Server. There is no R2 bucket or queue in between. Cloudflare returns `250 OK` to the remote sender only after MailPlus accepts the message. If your NAS is temporarily offline or rebooting, the Worker returns a temporary error (`421`) so the remote sending server retries automatically on its own schedule. ### 2. Sending mail (Outbound: MailPlus → Local Relay → Cloudflare → Internet) 1. **Cloudflare Email Sending** onboards your Cloudflare-hosted domain and automatically adds the required `cf-bounce` MX, SPF, DKIM, and `_dmarc` DNS records on Cloudflare. 2. **Built-in Local SMTP Relay (`127.0.0.1:2525`):** MailPlus Server's SMTP relay client uses `STARTTLS`, whereas Cloudflare Email Sending (`smtp.mx.cloudflare.net:465`) strictly requires **implicit TLS (SMTPS)** on port 465 authenticated with username `api_token` and your Cloudflare API token. MailPlus Setup Assistant runs a lightweight loopback-only relay (`127.0.0.1:2525`) that accepts STARTTLS + generated local credentials from MailPlus and streams the message straight to `smtp.mx.cloudflare.net:465` over TLS 1.2+. **No Cloudflare Tunnel is needed for outbound sending.** 3. **MailPlus keeps ownership of the queue:** The local relay does not spool messages or run a second retry queue. It returns `250 OK` to MailPlus only after Cloudflare confirms `250 OK`; any temporary upstream failure returns `451` so MailPlus's own queue handles retries cleanly. --- ## Why Use MailPlus Setup Assistant? - **No fixed IP or dedicated IP required:** Works behind residential routers, dynamic IPs, and CGNAT without opening port 25 on your router. - **No IP reputation or PTR headaches:** Because Cloudflare handles the internet-facing mail leg, you skip ISP port 25 blocks, residential IP blocklists, IP warm-up, and ISP reverse DNS (PTR) requests. - **Keep the real MailPlus UI:** Continue using Synology MailPlus webmail, MailPlus mobile apps, and standard IMAP/SMTP clients with zero workflow changes. - **Free App, free receiving, low-cost outbound sending:** - **MailPlus Setup Assistant** itself is free (and pairs with MailPlus Server's 5 free user licenses). - **Receiving mail through Cloudflare is completely free** (unlimited inbound mail on Cloudflare Email Routing, Workers VPC free during open beta, Cloudflare Tunnel included on Zero Trust Free). - **Sending mail to external addresses through Cloudflare** only needs Cloudflare's low-cost **Workers Paid plan (US$5/month, including 3,000 emails/month, then $0.35 per 1,000 emails)** — or if you already have a fixed IP with port 25 open, the wizard can configure direct delivery instead. - **Safe preview, rollback, and one-click removal:** Every Cloudflare and MailPlus change is previewed before anything is written, existing settings are snapshotted for rollback, and every created Cloudflare resource is tagged so pressing **Remove…** cleans up only what this App created. --- ## Prerequisites Before starting the setup wizard, make sure you have: 1. **Your domain hosted on Cloudflare DNS** (an active Full-setup zone in your Cloudflare account). 2. **For receiving mail through Cloudflare:** **[Syno Connect Center](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoPkgConnect/)** installed and connected to Cloudflare with **Sign in to Cloudflare and connect** using **that same Cloudflare account and that same domain** *(do not use "Get a temporary address"; see FAQ if you already run your own `cloudflared` tunnel)*. **Sending-only setups do not require a Tunnel.** 3. **Synology MailPlus Server** installed, running, and configured with your mail domain and at least one active user (Package Center → MailPlus Server). 4. **For sending mail to external recipients through Cloudflare:** Your Cloudflare account on the **Workers Paid plan** (US$5/month). *(Receiving-only setups work on Cloudflare's Workers Free plan.)* 5. A **DSM administrator account** to sign in and run the wizard. --- ## Installation and Step-by-Step Setup ### Step 1: Install and Connect Syno Connect Center (Required for Receiving) If you plan to **receive mail through Cloudflare**, set up your Cloudflare Tunnel with **[Syno Connect Center](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoPkgConnect/)** first. Since MailPlus Setup Assistant already requires your domain to be on Cloudflare DNS, **you can reuse that exact same domain directly in Connect** — no second domain is needed. 1. **Install [Syno Connect Center](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoPkgConnect/)** from Package Center (under the Syno Package Land package source) and open it. 2. Choose **Cloudflare**, then use **Sign in to Cloudflare and connect** to connect your own domain: - Sign in with the **same Cloudflare account** and pick the **same domain** you will use for MailPlus (for example, pick a name like `nas` on `example.com`). - **Do NOT choose "Get a temporary address" (quick tunnel):** A quick tunnel is anonymous and does not live inside your Cloudflare account, so MailPlus Setup Assistant cannot find or bind to it. 3. **Wait until the Tunnel shows healthy / connected** in Syno Connect Center before continuing (or if you already had MailPlus Setup Assistant open, return to the wizard and refresh / re-preview once the Tunnel is healthy). > **Good to know before connecting your own domain in Syno Connect Center:** > Connecting an own domain in Syno Connect Center also publishes your DSM sign-in page on a hostname under that domain (for example `nas.example.com`), making DSM reachable from the internet. Syno Connect Center will ask you to enable **2-step verification** and **Auto Block** in DSM first (and also lets you optionally restrict the web address with Cloudflare Access). - **Sending only?** You can skip Step 1 — outbound sending through Cloudflare does **not** need Syno Connect Center or a Tunnel. - **Also verify:** Your domain is active on Cloudflare DNS and **Synology MailPlus Server** is installed and running with your mail domain created. - *(Advanced: Already running your own self-managed `cloudflared` tunnel in the same Cloudflare account? See the FAQ below.)* ### Step 2: Install MailPlus Setup Assistant Install **[MailPlus Setup Assistant](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoMailPlusSetupAssistant/)** from Package Center (under the Syno Package Land package source) and open it from the DSM main menu. The **Overview** page shows your **MailPlus Server** status, **Set up mail**, any domains already configured **On Cloudflare** (along with the collapsible **How Cloudflare mail works** interactive diagram), **Diagnose mail**, and the **Mail relay** status and toggle. ![Overview page showing MailPlus Server status, Set up mail, configured Cloudflare domain, collapsible How Cloudflare mail works section, Diagnose mail, and Mail relay](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/766eae5e-2e70-4565-adac-abde1eb2faa7) ### Step 3: Start the Setup Wizard and Connect Cloudflare Click **Start** next to **Set up mail**, choose what you want to set up (**Send and receive**, **Receive only**, or **Send only**), and select **Use Cloudflare**. On the **Sign in to Cloudflare** step: 1. Click **Create the token on Cloudflare** — this opens Cloudflare's API token form with the 8 required permissions pre-filled (Zone Read, DNS Write, Email Sending Write, Zone Settings Write, Email Routing Rules Write, Workers Scripts Write, Connectivity Directory Admin, and Cloudflare Tunnel Read). 2. In Cloudflare, pick your account and zone (you can narrow **Zone Resources** to just your mail domain's zone), create the token, and copy it. 3. Paste the token into the **API token** field. It is encrypted immediately on your NAS and never displayed again. ### Step 4: Pick Your Domain and Choose How Mail Travels Select your Cloudflare-hosted domain and matching MailPlus domain. The wizard runs a read-only check of your MailPlus Server, DNS records, and your Syno Connect Center Cloudflare Tunnel, then asks **How mail travels**: - **Cloudflare receives and sends for me (recommended):** Works anywhere with no fixed IP or open ports. - **Use my own IP to send and receive directly:** For servers with a fixed IP and port 25 open. *(If the wizard reports that no healthy Cloudflare Tunnel was found yet, finish Step 1 in Syno Connect Center using **Sign in to Cloudflare and connect** on the same Cloudflare account and domain, wait until the Tunnel shows healthy, then return to MailPlus Setup Assistant and run the preview again.)* ![How mail travels step comparing Cloudflare route and direct IP route with Cloudflare pricing note](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96aba593-afff-408e-86ef-79a378ca29df) ### Step 5: Choose Receiving Mode, Preview Every Change, and Apply If you enabled receiving through Cloudflare, pick either **Receive the whole domain automatically** (recommended — new MailPlus users work immediately) or **Chosen mailboxes** (exact per-user rules). Before changing anything, the wizard displays a plain-language summary of every Cloudflare and MailPlus action it will perform (creating the Worker, VPC Service, routing rules, sending domain, and MailPlus relay settings automatically), along with a **Details** breakdown and a reminder that existing settings are saved first so you can roll back if needed. ![Confirm changes preview step listing exact Cloudflare and MailPlus changes before applying](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b157adf8-6bfa-43b4-baf9-dc160f7f8305) Click **Apply**. The wizard applies the changes, verifies them, and lets you keep or roll back the result. Once kept, you can immediately send and receive mail from MailPlus as usual. ### Step 6: Built-in Mail Diagnostics If mail ever bounces, lands in spam, or stops arriving, click **Start** next to **Diagnose mail** on the Overview page. Pick the symptom you are seeing and the assistant inspects MailPlus Server, DNS records, certificates, and network status — then tells you what is wrong and gives a direct button to fix it. ![Mail diagnostic results showing a detected issue with plain-language explanation and fix button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12015988-13c4-4d64-8bc7-c4c66852cf2a) --- ## Cloudflare Pricing & Official Limits All figures below are verified from official Cloudflare documentation (checked November 2026). Always refer to Cloudflare's linked pages for the latest quotas and pricing. | Area | Cloudflare Limit / Pricing | Notes | Official Source | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Inbound email volume (Email Routing)** | **Unlimited** (Free & Paid plans) | Receiving mail via Email Routing has no per-message fee | [Email Service Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/pricing/) | | **Outbound email pricing (Email Sending)** | **Workers Free:** Free, **verified destination addresses only**
**Workers Paid (US$5/mo):** **3,000 emails/month** included, then **$0.35 per 1,000 emails** | Sending to arbitrary external recipients requires Workers Paid; quota is per account per billing cycle | [Email Service Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/pricing/) · [Workers Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/) | | **Daily outbound sending limit** | **Dynamic per account** (no fixed public number) | New accounts start with a conservative daily quota that scales automatically with reputation; request higher limits via Cloudflare's form if needed (returns SMTP `451 4.7.1` when reached) | [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | | **Max message size (incl. attachments)** | **25 MiB** (inbound & outbound) | Applies after MIME encoding; MailPlus Server may enforce a lower limit if configured | [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) · [SMTP Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/api/send-emails/smtp/) | | **Max recipients per email** | **50** (`To` + `Cc` + `Bcc` combined) | Enforced by both the local relay and Cloudflare | [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | | **Subject / custom headers** | **998 characters** subject / **16 KB** combined headers | RFC 5322 compliant | [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | | **Routing rules per domain** | **200** | Applies if using **Chosen mailboxes** mode; **Whole domain** mode avoids per-user rules | [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | | **Verified destination addresses** | **200** per account | Shared across all domains in the account | [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | | **Email domains per zone** | **30** (Email Routing + Email Sending combined, incl. apex) | Requires an active zone hosted on Cloudflare DNS | [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) · [Domain Configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/configuration/domains/) | | **Workers daily requests (inbound Worker)** | **Workers Free:** **100,000 requests/day**
**Workers Paid:** **10 million/month** included (+$0.30/million) | Each incoming email invokes the inbound Worker once | [Workers Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/) · [Workers Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/) | | **Workers CPU & memory per isolate** | **CPU:** 10 ms (Free) / up to 5 min (Paid, default 30 s)
**Memory:** 128 MB | Very large or slow handlers on Workers Free may hit `EXCEEDED_CPU` | [Workers Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/) · [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | | **Workers VPC Services** | **1,000 VPC Services** per account; **Free during Open Beta** | Available on both Workers Free and Paid plans; subject to change at GA | [Workers VPC Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/platform/limits/) · [Workers VPC Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/platform/pricing/) | | **Cloudflare Tunnels** | **1,000** `cloudflared` tunnels per account | Available on Zero Trust Free | [Cloudflare One Account Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/account-limits/) | | **Allowed email type** | **Transactional / personal mail only** | Bulk marketing emails are not allowed; must comply with CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CASL | [Email Service FAQ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/faq/) · [Email Service Limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/) | --- ## FAQ & Troubleshooting ### Why do I need Syno Connect Center for receiving mail, and why can't I use "Get a temporary address"? - **Receiving mail through Cloudflare** needs a Cloudflare Tunnel inside your Cloudflare account so Cloudflare can reach MailPlus Server on your NAS without opening router port 25. MailPlus Setup Assistant reuses the Tunnel from **[Syno Connect Center](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoPkgConnect/)** and never modifies or deletes it. - In Syno Connect Center, you must use **Sign in to Cloudflare and connect** with the **same Cloudflare account and the same domain** you use for MailPlus. **Do not choose "Get a temporary address" (quick tunnel)** — a quick tunnel is not registered under your Cloudflare account, so MailPlus Setup Assistant cannot see it. - Once the Tunnel shows healthy in Syno Connect Center, return to MailPlus Setup Assistant and run the preview again. - **Sending mail through Cloudflare** does **not** require Syno Connect Center or any Cloudflare Tunnel. ### Does connecting my domain in Syno Connect Center expose DSM to the internet? **Yes.** When Syno Connect Center connects your own domain, it opens DSM on a hostname under that domain (for example `nas.example.com`) so DSM is reachable from the internet. Because of that, Syno Connect Center asks you to enable **2-step verification** and **Auto Block** in DSM before connecting. (In Syno Connect Center, you can also optionally restrict the web address to an email allow-list with Cloudflare Access.) ### Advanced: Can I use my own self-managed `cloudflared` Tunnel instead of Syno Connect Center? **Yes.** If you prefer not to expose DSM through Syno Connect Center — or if you already run your own `cloudflared` tunnel on your NAS (or on the same LAN) under the **same Cloudflare account** — MailPlus Setup Assistant discovers any healthy Cloudflare Tunnel in that account read-only and binds its Workers VPC Service to your NAS's private LAN IPv4 on TCP port 25. Your existing `cloudflared` configuration and routes are left untouched. ### Do I have to set up or maintain the Cloudflare Worker and VPC Service myself? **No.** MailPlus Setup Assistant automatically creates, configures, and binds both the Inbound Email Worker and the Workers VPC Service inside your Cloudflare account during setup. You do not need to touch the Workers dashboard, and clicking **Remove…** in the App cleans them up automatically. ### Does my domain have to be hosted on Cloudflare? **Yes.** Both Cloudflare Email Routing (receiving) and Cloudflare Email Sending (sending) require your domain to be an active zone managed on **Cloudflare DNS** (Full setup). Because your domain is already on Cloudflare DNS, you can reuse that same domain directly in Syno Connect Center too. ### What does this actually cost? Can I use Cloudflare's Free plan? - **MailPlus Setup Assistant:** Free (and Synology MailPlus Server includes 5 free user licenses). - **Receiving mail through Cloudflare:** **Free** on Cloudflare's Free plan (unlimited inbound emails on Email Routing, 100,000 Worker requests/day on Workers Free, Workers VPC free during open beta, Cloudflare Tunnel included on Zero Trust Free). - **Sending mail to external addresses through Cloudflare:** Requires Cloudflare's **Workers Paid plan (US$5/month)**, which includes **3,000 outbound emails/month**, then **$0.35 per 1,000 emails**. On Workers Free, Cloudflare Email Sending only sends to verified destination addresses in your account and refuses other external recipients with `550 5.7.1`. If you already have a fixed IP with port 25 open, you can choose the direct-IP route instead. ### What happens to incoming mail if my NAS is offline or rebooting? Nothing is stored in Cloudflare. When the inbound Worker cannot reach MailPlus over your tunnel, Cloudflare answers the remote mail server with a temporary SMTP error (`421`). Standard mail servers automatically retry delivery over the next several hours, and the message arrives once your NAS is back online. ### I added a new MailPlus user, and they aren't receiving email Check the **On Cloudflare** section on the Overview page: - If your domain uses **Whole domain, automatically**, new MailPlus users start receiving mail immediately with no extra step. - If your domain uses **Chosen mailboxes**, click **Sync mailboxes** after adding or removing users in MailPlus Server. ### How do I cleanly undo the Cloudflare setup? Open MailPlus Setup Assistant and click **Remove…** next to your domain under **On Cloudflare** *before* uninstalling the package. Uninstalling the package from Package Center intentionally keeps your Cloudflare settings intact so you don't accidentally break live mail. The **Remove…** dialog deletes only the DNS records, routing rules, Worker, VPC Service, and local token created by this App, and restores your previous MailPlus settings. Your Syno Connect Center tunnel is never touched. ### What happens if I revoke or expire my Cloudflare API token? Because the local SMTP relay authenticates to `smtp.mx.cloudflare.net:465` using that API token, revoking it stops outbound mail and prevents **Sync mailboxes** or **Remove…** from working. You can paste a replacement token directly from the prompt under **On Cloudflare** on the Overview page. ### Why did an outgoing email fail with a size or recipient error? Both the local relay and Cloudflare enforce a **25 MiB** total message size limit (including MIME-encoded attachments — roughly ~18 MiB of raw file attachments) and a maximum of **50 recipients** (`To`, `Cc`, and `Bcc` combined) per message. Split large attachments or use a Drive share link instead. ### Can I send marketing newsletters with this setup? No. Cloudflare's official [Email Service FAQ](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/faq/) states that Email Service supports transactional email only — marketing blasts can degrade account reputation or trigger rejections.

Prerequisites

Before starting the setup wizard, make sure you have:

  1. Your domain hosted on Cloudflare DNS (an active Full-setup zone in your Cloudflare account).
  2. For receiving mail through Cloudflare: Syno Connect Center installed and connected to Cloudflare with Sign in to Cloudflare and connect using that same Cloudflare account and that same domain (do not use "Get a temporary address"; see FAQ if you already run your own cloudflared tunnel). Sending-only setups do not require a Tunnel.
  3. Synology MailPlus Server installed, running, and configured with your mail domain and at least one active user (Package Center → MailPlus Server).
  4. For sending mail to external recipients through Cloudflare: Your Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan (US$5/month). (Receiving-only setups work on Cloudflare's Workers Free plan.)
  5. A DSM administrator account to sign in and run the wizard.

Installation and Step-by-Step Setup

Step 1: Install and Connect Syno Connect Center (Required for Receiving)

If you plan to receive mail through Cloudflare, set up your Cloudflare Tunnel with Syno Connect Center first. Since MailPlus Setup Assistant already requires your domain to be on Cloudflare DNS, you can reuse that exact same domain directly in Connect — no second domain is needed.

  1. Install Syno Connect Center from Package Center (under the Syno Package Land package source) and open it.
  2. Choose Cloudflare, then use Sign in to Cloudflare and connect to connect your own domain:
    • Sign in with the same Cloudflare account and pick the same domain you will use for MailPlus (for example, pick a name like nas on example.com).
    • Do NOT choose "Get a temporary address" (quick tunnel): A quick tunnel is anonymous and does not live inside your Cloudflare account, so MailPlus Setup Assistant cannot find or bind to it.
  3. Wait until the Tunnel shows healthy / connected in Syno Connect Center before continuing (or if you already had MailPlus Setup Assistant open, return to the wizard and refresh / re-preview once the Tunnel is healthy).

Good to know before connecting your own domain in Syno Connect Center:
Connecting an own domain in Syno Connect Center also publishes your DSM sign-in page on a hostname under that domain (for example nas.example.com), making DSM reachable from the internet. Syno Connect Center will ask you to enable 2-step verification and Auto Block in DSM first (and also lets you optionally restrict the web address with Cloudflare Access).

  • Sending only? You can skip Step 1 — outbound sending through Cloudflare does not need Syno Connect Center or a Tunnel.
  • Also verify: Your domain is active on Cloudflare DNS and Synology MailPlus Server is installed and running with your mail domain created.
  • (Advanced: Already running your own self-managed cloudflared tunnel in the same Cloudflare account? See the FAQ below.)

Step 2: Install MailPlus Setup Assistant

Install MailPlus Setup Assistant from Package Center (under the Syno Package Land package source) and open it from the DSM main menu.

The Overview page shows your MailPlus Server status, Set up mail, any domains already configured On Cloudflare (along with the collapsible How Cloudflare mail works interactive diagram), Diagnose mail, and the Mail relay status and toggle.

Step 3: Start the Setup Wizard and Connect Cloudflare

Click Start next to Set up mail, choose what you want to set up (Send and receive, Receive only, or Send only), and select Use Cloudflare.

On the Sign in to Cloudflare step:

  1. Click Create the token on Cloudflare — this opens Cloudflare's API token form with the 8 required permissions pre-filled (Zone Read, DNS Write, Email Sending Write, Zone Settings Write, Email Routing Rules Write, Workers Scripts Write, Connectivity Directory Admin, and Cloudflare Tunnel Read).
  2. In Cloudflare, pick your account and zone (you can narrow Zone Resources to just your mail domain's zone), create the token, and copy it.
  3. Paste the token into the API token field. It is encrypted immediately on your NAS and never displayed again.

Step 4: Pick Your Domain and Choose How Mail Travels

Select your Cloudflare-hosted domain and matching MailPlus domain. The wizard runs a read-only check of your MailPlus Server, DNS records, and your Syno Connect Center Cloudflare Tunnel, then asks How mail travels:

  • Cloudflare receives and sends for me (recommended): Works anywhere with no fixed IP or open ports.
  • Use my own IP to send and receive directly: For servers with a fixed IP and port 25 open.

(If the wizard reports that no healthy Cloudflare Tunnel was found yet, finish Step 1 in Syno Connect Center using Sign in to Cloudflare and connect on the same Cloudflare account and domain, wait until the Tunnel shows healthy, then return to MailPlus Setup Assistant and run the preview again.)

Step 5: Choose Receiving Mode, Preview Every Change, and Apply

If you enabled receiving through Cloudflare, pick either Receive the whole domain automatically (recommended — new MailPlus users work immediately) or Chosen mailboxes (exact per-user rules).

Before changing anything, the wizard displays a plain-language summary of every Cloudflare and MailPlus action it will perform (creating the Worker, VPC Service, routing rules, sending domain, and MailPlus relay settings automatically), along with a Details breakdown and a reminder that existing settings are saved first so you can roll back if needed.

Click Apply. The wizard applies the changes, verifies them, and lets you keep or roll back the result. Once kept, you can immediately send and receive mail from MailPlus as usual.

Step 6: Built-in Mail Diagnostics

If mail ever bounces, lands in spam, or stops arriving, click Start next to Diagnose mail on the Overview page. Pick the symptom you are seeing and the assistant inspects MailPlus Server, DNS records, certificates, and network status — then tells you what is wrong and gives a direct button to fix it.

FAQ & Troubleshooting

Why do I need Syno Connect Center for receiving mail, and why can't I use "Get a temporary address"?

  • Receiving mail through Cloudflare needs a Cloudflare Tunnel inside your Cloudflare account so Cloudflare can reach MailPlus Server on your NAS without opening router port 25. MailPlus Setup Assistant reuses the Tunnel from Syno Connect Center and never modifies or deletes it.
  • In Syno Connect Center, you must use Sign in to Cloudflare and connect with the same Cloudflare account and the same domain you use for MailPlus. Do not choose "Get a temporary address" (quick tunnel) — a quick tunnel is not registered under your Cloudflare account, so MailPlus Setup Assistant cannot see it.
  • Once the Tunnel shows healthy in Syno Connect Center, return to MailPlus Setup Assistant and run the preview again.
  • Sending mail through Cloudflare does not require Syno Connect Center or any Cloudflare Tunnel.

Does connecting my domain in Syno Connect Center expose DSM to the internet?

Yes. When Syno Connect Center connects your own domain, it opens DSM on a hostname under that domain (for example nas.example.com) so DSM is reachable from the internet. Because of that, Syno Connect Center asks you to enable 2-step verification and Auto Block in DSM before connecting. (In Syno Connect Center, you can also optionally restrict the web address to an email allow-list with Cloudflare Access.)

Advanced: Can I use my own self-managed cloudflared Tunnel instead of Syno Connect Center?

Yes. If you prefer not to expose DSM through Syno Connect Center — or if you already run your own cloudflared tunnel on your NAS (or on the same LAN) under the same Cloudflare account — MailPlus Setup Assistant discovers any healthy Cloudflare Tunnel in that account read-only and binds its Workers VPC Service to your NAS's private LAN IPv4 on TCP port 25. Your existing cloudflared configuration and routes are left untouched.

Do I have to set up or maintain the Cloudflare Worker and VPC Service myself?

No. MailPlus Setup Assistant automatically creates, configures, and binds both the Inbound Email Worker and the Workers VPC Service inside your Cloudflare account during setup. You do not need to touch the Workers dashboard, and clicking Remove… in the App cleans them up automatically.

Does my domain have to be hosted on Cloudflare?

Yes. Both Cloudflare Email Routing (receiving) and Cloudflare Email Sending (sending) require your domain to be an active zone managed on Cloudflare DNS (Full setup). Because your domain is already on Cloudflare DNS, you can reuse that same domain directly in Syno Connect Center too.

What does this actually cost? Can I use Cloudflare's Free plan?

  • MailPlus Setup Assistant: Free (and Synology MailPlus Server includes 5 free user licenses).
  • Receiving mail through Cloudflare: Free on Cloudflare's Free plan (unlimited inbound emails on Email Routing, 100,000 Worker requests/day on Workers Free, Workers VPC free during open beta, Cloudflare Tunnel included on Zero Trust Free).
  • Sending mail to external addresses through Cloudflare: Requires Cloudflare's Workers Paid plan (US$5/month), which includes 3,000 outbound emails/month, then $0.35 per 1,000 emails. On Workers Free, Cloudflare Email Sending only sends to verified destination addresses in your account and refuses other external recipients with 550 5.7.1. If you already have a fixed IP with port 25 open, you can choose the direct-IP route instead.

What happens to incoming mail if my NAS is offline or rebooting?

Nothing is stored in Cloudflare. When the inbound Worker cannot reach MailPlus over your tunnel, Cloudflare answers the remote mail server with a temporary SMTP error (421). Standard mail servers automatically retry delivery over the next several hours, and the message arrives once your NAS is back online.

I added a new MailPlus user, and they aren't receiving email

Check the On Cloudflare section on the Overview page:

  • If your domain uses Whole domain, automatically, new MailPlus users start receiving mail immediately with no extra step.
  • If your domain uses Chosen mailboxes, click Sync mailboxes after adding or removing users in MailPlus Server.

How do I cleanly undo the Cloudflare setup?

Open MailPlus Setup Assistant and click Remove… next to your domain under On Cloudflare before uninstalling the package. Uninstalling the package from Package Center intentionally keeps your Cloudflare settings intact so you don't accidentally break live mail. The Remove… dialog deletes only the DNS records, routing rules, Worker, VPC Service, and local token created by this App, and restores your previous MailPlus settings. Your Syno Connect Center tunnel is never touched.

What happens if I revoke or expire my Cloudflare API token?

Because the local SMTP relay authenticates to smtp.mx.cloudflare.net:465 using that API token, revoking it stops outbound mail and prevents Sync mailboxes or Remove… from working. You can paste a replacement token directly from the prompt under On Cloudflare on the Overview page.

Why did an outgoing email fail with a size or recipient error?

Both the local relay and Cloudflare enforce a 25 MiB total message size limit (including MIME-encoded attachments — roughly ~18 MiB of raw file attachments) and a maximum of 50 recipients (To, Cc, and Bcc combined) per message. Split large attachments or use a Drive share link instead.

Can I send marketing newsletters with this setup?

No. Cloudflare's official Email Service FAQ states that Email Service supports transactional email only — marketing blasts can degrade account reputation or trigger rejections.
